back: Measuring the amplitude of an analogue sound wave at regular time intervals and storing each measurement in binary.
The number of samples taken per second, in hertz (Hz).
The number of bits used to store each sample; n bits give 2^n possible values.
Size (bits) = sampling rate × sampling resolution × time (seconds) × number of channels. Divide by 8 for bytes.

front: Effect of a higher sampling rate or resolution
back: A more accurate recording but a larger file.

front: Effect of a very low sampling rate
back: High-frequency sounds are lost or reproduced at the wrong pitch.
Mono has one channel; stereo has two, so a stereo file is twice the size of the same mono recording.
A signal that varies continuously, such as a sound wave. A digital signal is a sequence of binary numbers.

front: Unit trap in sound size questions
back: The rate is per second, so convert minutes to seconds before multiplying.
